messages:
sahil: saw a customer escalation (C-18923) about p99 latency jumping ~600ms after last canary deploy. Happened ~10:05 UTC. Noticed in prod routing cohort A only :thinking:
mona: pulling traces + flamegraphs now, sending p95/p99 dashboards. Can we confirm only runtime version v2.17 is in the canary pool?
deploy-bot: deployment v2.17 -> canary group alpha rolled at 2025-10-21T10:01:12Z (rollout id r-88f3)
alex: yes v2.17 included the late-binding kernel selector change (prefer-latebound=true) and a small kv-cache eviction tweak. Those were meant to improve throughput on long seqs.
nate: looking at traces — spike is mostly in auth-bound hotpath: `AuthPermFetch` calls show KV cache miss ratio up ~8x for affected tenant cohort, especially cold-prefix requests.
clare: could be an interaction: late-binding kernel can increase transient memory usage per worker, which may shrink in-process KV cache size under pressure. If cache shrinks, cold-prefix latency goes up and that bubbles to p99.
sahil: repro plan? support has a curl example that hits the failing route. We should try against canary nodes.
mona: repro snippet from support: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"model":"open-rw-1","input":"<long prefix>...","max_tokens":32}'
```

mona: I'm running that looped against canary IPs now, adding `X-Debug-KV:1` header to get cache stats.
alex: quick mitigation options: 1) flip prefer-latebound=false on canary runtime config 2) increase kv-cache-limit per-worker 3) route traffic away from canary cohort for model open-rw-1 until we bisect.
oncall: customer impact is moderate (several tickets), recommend immediate traffic shift to stable for the affected cohort while we bisect. I'll coordinate. :thumbsup:
support-bot: noted tickets C-18923, C-18927, C-18930 flagged; informing account team.
nate: bisect suggestion: isolate the two changes (kernel late-bound + cache eviction tweak). We can re-deploy a variant with late-bound disabled but keep eviction tweak, and vice versa. I can spin variants `v2.17a` and `v2.17b` in staging then promote to a small canary subset.
clare: also want to capture per-worker resident set + kv-cache slots during repro. Add env `KV_DEBUG=1` for a short window. Watch for OOMs if we bump cache size.
sahil: temporary config change to prefer-latebound=false on canary would be fastest. How to flip?
alex: patch command: 
```bash
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"prefer-latebound":"false"}}' || true
# then rollout restart runtime-deployment-canary
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/runtime-canary
```

mona: I've applied `KV_DEBUG=1` annotation to canary pods and started the curl loop. Early results: cache miss rate dropped after flip to prefer-latebound=false, p99 back down ~350ms within 3 minutes.
oncall: routing change executed: moved 60% of alpha cohort traffic back to stable cluster via routing-policy `cohort-surge-guard`.
support-bot: update sent to customers: "We've routed traffic to stable and are investigating a config interaction; minimal service disruption expected."
sahil: next steps: nate to run the two-way bisect, alex/clare to prepare a safe kv-cache size increase param, mona to collect traces for 10 minutes post-fix, oncall to keep routing guard for 1h.
nate: starting bisect job now. I'll post progress updates. If bisect points to late-bound as root cause, we should roll that change back in next stable patch.
clare: filing follow-up postmortem ticket PM-4921 with action items: better integ test for kv-cache under late-binding, add canary perf test that runs auth-heavy synthetic workload.
sahil: thanks all. tagging @oncall if anything regresses. :eyes:
oncall: standing by, will escalate to infra if memory pressure shows up.
